Lessons.Title: Reasoning about Exponential Graphs (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: recover growth/decay factor from two graph points with nonconsecutive inputs, interpret intersections of exponential graphs and distinguish a matching formula from a superficially plausible one. Original first-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 5 Lesson 13, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/13/preparation.html and student tasks https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/13/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source's special feature is nonconsecutive input intervals when inferring factors.

Original hypothetical device value graph has A(0)=320 dollars and A(2)=180 dollars for A(t)=a·b^t. At0, a=320. At2,320b²=180 so b²=9/16, positive b=3/4=0.75. Therefore A(t)=320(.75)^t. It predicts A1=$240,A3=$135; do not mistakenly set factor to180/320=.5625, which is the TWO-year factor.

Original second comparison: F(t)=60·2^t, G(t)=240·(.5)^t, for whole nonnegative times. Equate:60·2^t=240·(1/2)^t; dividing yields4^t=4, so t=1, both outputs120. At t0 F60<G240; at t2 F240>G60. The intersection gives equality at the SAME input.

Student task: identify a,b from graphs with missing intermediate t, sketch both curves on shared axes, calculate an intersection and explain where ordering reverses. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for factor extraction, exact graph predictions, intersection and limitations and units.

KeyConcepts.Title: Factor over multiple steps
KeyConcepts.Definition: If f(t+k)/f(t)=b^k, infer b by taking kth root for positive b.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not confuse multi-step ratio with per-step b.

KeyConcepts.Title: Intersection of exponential curves
KeyConcepts.Definition: At crossing the two function values are equal for same input.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Taking a two-year ratio as annual factor
Comparing graph heights at mismatched x-values
CommonMistakes.Correction: Set functions equal at common t.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming a unique real-world device depreciation law
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Invented points alone don't establish a market process.

SummaryPoints: Use exponent difference to infer b from nonconsecutive points.
Intersection equality compares two outputs at one input.
Teacher reviews graph reasoning and contextual credibility.
